note: v1, LEAST COMMON: THE RULE, A SKELETON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 03:20-03:50 GMT). Not heard by me. WHAT IT IS: three clicks on cycles of 3, 5 and 7 sixteenths against a bass drum on every fourth; 126, G minor, 210 bars (6:40). Nothing else is written. Two clicks meeting make a ping (D5, B flat 4, F4), three a chord, three on the drum turn a page (every 26 bars and a beat, so on beat two, then three, then four), and all of it lands on the one once in 105 bars, which is half the song. The pings between two chords are a twelve-note tune that reads the same backwards, and nobody wrote it. The second half is the same rule one size up (3, 5 and 7 beats, each filled with the next one's number, Euclid's way): its meetings are a held tone, and from the seventh page the small tune comes back over it. The four's own parts (bass, off-beat hat, clap) arrive a page at a time; in the last 105 sixteenths of each half they drop out and the clicks walk to the one alone. The chord is Give or Take's with its ninth, for the seam. MEASURED: 84.64 / 84.32 (seeds 0 / 11); -13.1 LUFS, true peak -1.6; structure 75.4 (14 sections), variety 63.3, recurrence 100, spectrum 86.6. FIVE BUILDS IN THE TICK (68.9, 74.3, 82.4, 84.0, 84.6), each read part by part: the drum and a bass both on G1 put the mix 23 dB over the album's envelope at 44 Hz (bass up an octave, drum eq: now inside tolerance); the clicks were 20 to 26 dB under the mix and their peaks, not their level, were what the limiter held (a clip on each, then the fader: now 11 to 16 under); the hat was 42 dB under (now 15); the held tone at -17 dB was 94% of 250-500 Hz (now -28); the pings an octave higher read 15 dB over at 1.2 kHz. WHAT IS WEAK: it is flat (level range 2.8 dB; nothing changes inside a page but who is playing); 11 dB over the envelope at 750 Hz (the five's tock on G5) and 7 to 8 under at 133-182 Hz; no space, no effect driven by the numbers and no illusion yet. I cannot judge whether three clicks, a hat and a clap read as music or as a metronome, nor whether the page turns are heard as events.
next: v2 on, every change behind a switch (v1 has none). In order of what the song lacks: (1) THE MEETINGS AS EVENTS: they are only notes now. Let a page turn do something to the room (the hall opening on the chord and closing over the page; the clicks' echo time stepping to the cycle that just met). (2) SPACE BY NUMBER: each click's place from its phase in its own cycle (the three walks left to right every 3 x 16 sixteenths, the seven the other way), so a meeting is also heard as three sounds arriving at one place; keep it mono-safe. (3) DYNAMICS INSIDE A PAGE: level range is 2.8 dB. A slow ride on the clicks by distance to the next meeting (quieter far from it), and the bass drum's `rumble` growing through a page. (4) THE SPECTRUM: the five's tock on G5 is 48 to 77% of 500 Hz-1 kHz (11 dB over at 750 Hz): try it on D5 or a shorter decay; something at 133-182 Hz (the bass has only G2 and B flat 2). (5) AN ILLUSION that the rule gives for free: at the half, the cycles go from sixteenths to beats (a 4:1 slowing) while the tune stays; a Risset rhythm across that seam would make it sound like one continuous slowing. (6) The bass is a placeholder cell; let it be the three meetings' roots. Read alone before the mix: solo.sh / parts.py in ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t2-v1/.

v2, WHAT A MEETING DOES (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 05:50-06:13 GMT). Not heard by me. In v1 a meeting was only a note. Six switches (--without-place, -near, -door, -memory, -roots, -break); all six off is v1 byte for byte. Each is driven by one count, how far it is to the next time all three clicks meet. (1) PLACE: the three walks out to the left and back between two meetings of all three, the five to the right, the seven stays, so a chord is three sounds arriving at one place. Alone, half way: the three 11 dB to the left, the five 12 to the right; it is pan only, the mono sum loses 0.1 dB. (2) NEAR: the clicks are loudest where the three meet, 5 dB quieter half way. (3) THE DOOR: a far room behind the clicks, shut when a page turns, a step more open each time the three meet, wide open before the next page. (4) MEMORY: a click keeps the note of the last meeting it was in: the five's tock on G4, D4 or F4 (128, 651 and 126 strokes), the seven's knock on G3, B flat 3 or F3; two tunes nobody wrote, an octave under the pings. (5) ROOTS: the bass keeps its rhythm and takes the note of the last meeting of any two (G2, D2, B flat 2, F2), on a sine with its octave. (6) THE BREAK: before each page of the first half turns, from the last time the five and the seven meet (35 sixteenths), the four stops and the clicks walk to the turn alone, the door wide open: 6 to 9 dB down, then the page turns on the drum. SCORE 94.02 and 93.97 on two seeds; v1 re-read on the same pin today 85.94 (it was published at 84.64). Spectrum 86.6 to 97.2 (v1 was 11 dB over the envelope at 750 Hz and 7 to 8 under at 133-182 Hz; now 547 Hz is 7.8 over and nothing else is beyond 7), variety 63.3 to 75.1 (level range 2.8 to 5.2 dB), structure 75.4 to 99.8, recurrence 100 to 98.9, cohesion 100 to 93.0. SEVEN BUILDS (88.2, 89.2 / 86.0, 80.0, 87.4, 87.0, 93.8, 94.0), read part by part. What they found: the tock on the pings' own octave stacked with them (13 dB over at 547 Hz), an octave over them it was 12 over at 1.2 kHz; under them it is inside. The bass with D on D3 left the low octave 8 to 10 dB short; all four notes low with an octave layer filled both. That new bass patch was 14 dB louder than the sine it replaced: for one build the bass stood 3 dB over the bass drum and the clicks fell 4 to 9 dB against the mix (it read 87.4, spectrum 99); the bass went down 6 dB and the tock up 3 (bass now 5.4 under the mix, drum 2.7, clicks 14 to 19). WHAT IS WEAK: the section count (27) is at the top edge of the scorer's range, and with one more the structure term falls to 76: the score is on a knife's edge and I did not aim at it. The far room adds only about 0.6 dB to the whole where the clicks are alone, so the door may be faint under the four. The five's tock is two octaves and a fourth lower than v1's on most strokes (G5 then, D4 now): it may no longer read as a click. The seven is 15 to 19 dB under the mix. I cannot judge whether the walk is heard as movement or only as a click getting quieter, nor whether the two tunes read as tunes.
next: v3 on, every change behind a switch (v2 has place, near, door, memory, roots, break). (1) THE HALF-WAY SEAM (the illusion the rule gives for free): at the half the cycles go from sixteenths to beats, a 4:1 slowing, while the tune stays. A Risset rhythm across the last stretch of the first half (the clicks' level handed from the sixteenth cycles to the beat cycles while both run) would make it one continuous slowing. Borrow the arithmetic from Hearing Things' risset(). (2) THE DOOR IS FAINT: +0.6 dB where the clicks are alone. Send the pings and the chord through it as well, or let the door change the room's size (decay by step) and not only its level. (3) THE TOCK: on D4 for 651 strokes; is it still a click. Try the bar struck harder and damped at 15 ms, or the three notes spread over two octaves by which partner it met (up for the three, down for the seven) at a lower level. (4) THE SECOND HALF has no break of its own size and its door moves only four times: one size up may be too slow to hear. Try the walk and the door at the half's size AND the small size together (the same tune at two sizes, as the pings already are). (5) 547 Hz is 7.8 over: the pings on D5 and the chord. (6) THE SEVEN is the quietest thing (15 to 19 under). (7) Sections: 27 found, the top of the range; do not add more small boundaries. Evidence and helpers: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t2-v2/ (solo2.sh has a window with the door open; ab.sh renders a stretch with and without a switch).

v3, THE SPRING (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 07:50-08:16 GMT). Not heard by me. Eight switches (--without-rundown, -windup, -line, -rest, -swing, -through, -wide, -seven; all eight off is v2 byte for byte). (1) RUNDOWN: in the last stretch of the first half (105 sixteenths, the four already stopped) each click loses every other stroke, then every other again: cycles of 3, 5, 7 sixteenths, then eighths, then beats, 3 against 5 against 7 at every size, down to the second half's size. Pings follow the quieter of the two that meet. The stretch by quarter: -27.9 -37.4 -40.1 -43.1 dB (v2: -27.8 -34.8 -34.4 -33.9). (2) WINDUP: in the song's last stretch the big cycles lose their fillings and the small ones come back the same way backwards; home is reached at the size the song began at. (3) LINE: in the second half the bass goes on following the SMALL cycles' meetings: 177 changes of note where it had 46. (4) REST: three breaks in the second half, one size up (60 sixteenths before each page turn, bars 128, 154, 181): the four stops, 9.6 dB down, back on the turn. (5) SWING: the door opens through each stretch, not in steps. (6) THROUGH and WIDE: pings, chord and tone sent to the far room; the room 6 dB up, hp 900. (7) The seven 1.5 dB up. SCORE 95.64 and 95.91 on two seeds; v2 re-read today 94.37 (one seed). Sections 27 (the top of the scorer's range) to 14 and 13; variety 75.1 to 81.1; recurrence share 0.70 (its ceiling) to 0.66 and 0.61; spectrum 97.2 to 95.7: 547 Hz 7.8 over to 6.7, but 114 Hz 6.6 under to 9.3 under. FIVE BUILDS. (a) rundown, windup, through, seven: 86.3: one borderline boundary more (28) and the recurrence share over its band. (b) + swing: 91.2. (c) + line: 96.5, 10 and 9 sections, near the range's floor. (d) + rest, the room 6 dB up at hp 500: 95.1 and 95.3; the door at last measurable (2.6 dB in page 3's break) but 547 and 641 Hz 9 dB over. (e) hp 900, the seven 1.5: published. WHAT IS WEAK: THE DOOR IS STILL FAINT: in the published build it moves page 3's break 0.7 dB above 1.2 kHz and nothing under; THROUGH and WIDE are close to unheard, as the door was in v2. THE WINDUP IS THINNER, NOT FULLER: 2 to 4 dB less above 5 kHz through the stretch than v2's, because the fillings were more strokes than the small cycles are; whether it reads as winding up I cannot tell. The recurrence share is 0.04 under its ceiling on one seed. The low end is 2 dB down beside the rest (114 Hz 9.3 under). SWING and LINE were measured only by the scorer. I published (e) under (c)'s score for the second half's breaks and the wider margin in sections. I cannot judge whether the rundown is heard as one clock slowing or as clicks dropping out.
next: v4 on, every change behind a switch (v3 has rundown, windup, line, rest, swing, through, wide, seven on top of v2's six). (1) THE DOOR, third time: level does not carry it (0.6 dB in v2, 0.7 now; at hp 500 and +6 dB it was heard but put 547 and 641 Hz 9 dB over). Make it a change of SIZE or DISTANCE, not level: the far room's pre-delay and decay by step, or the clicks' dry level ridden DOWN as the door opens (they go away; the room stays). Measure on page 3's break (288b-316b, ab3.sh / ab5.sh). (2) THE WINDUP is thinner than what it replaces: keep the fillings to the half-way point, or wind up on the pings' level as well so the tune swells into home. (3) THE LOW END: 114 Hz is 9.3 under; the bass fader 1.5 dB up, or B flat 2 doubled an octave down. (4) THE RUNDOWN is 13 seconds: try it over two stretches, the first with the four still in, and ask one by-ear card: one clock slowing, or clicks dropping out. (5) THE SECOND HALF now reads as three sections in 105 bars beside the breaks: give page 7 something of its own (the hat's off-beat moved a sixteenth each page, by rule). (6) The tock (651 strokes on D4) and the seam to Standing Room: the last stretch changed, so re-render seam 2 for the mixplan. v4, THE CLICKS GO THROUGH THE DOOR (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 09:50-10:10 GMT). Not heard by me. Five switches (--without-away, -home, -slow, -push, -low; all five off is v3 byte for byte). (1) AWAY: the door was a room getting louder behind clicks that stayed put (0.7 dB in three rounds). Now the clicks' own sound falls as the door opens, 9 dB by the last step, and what the far room gives back of them holds: they have their own far room (bus `gone`) whose fader makes up what theirs lose. Read on the three clicks alone, raw, with the far rooms and without (dr.sh): in the third page's break v3's clicks stood 1.8 dB OVER their far room, v4's 7.2 UNDER; two bars after the page turn both are the same (the room shut). In the mastered mix the break reads -26.2 dB (v3 -22.8) and, above 5 kHz, -38.9 against -31.0 for the two bars after the turn (v3 -31.3, -30.7): the page turn is now a step of 8 dB in the clicks' band. One size up in the second half: a step further a page (above 5 kHz by page -34.9 -37.0 -33.4 -33.5; v3 -32.9 -32.8 -30.8 -31.4). (2) HOME: over the last stretch the clicks walk back to the front, the pings swell 3 dB, and the big cycles' fillings stay whole to the half-way point. Above 5 kHz by quarter -34.9 -35.3 -37.1 -33.7 against -33.5 for the stretch before (v3 -33.7 -35.8 -35.6 -32.2 against -31.4): the deepest dip is 3.6 dB where it was 4.4. (3) SLOW: the clock runs down over two stretches (from bar 92, 25 s), the first with the four still playing; while it runs down the clicks stand in front. By quarter stretch -13.4 -13.8 -13.7 -13.8, then -17.3 -29.4 -32.9 -33.1 (v3's one stretch -17.2 -25.9 -28.3 -31.3). (4) PUSH: on the last page of each half the hat is a sixteenth late (80 strokes a page on the fourth sixteenth of the beat). (5) LOW: the bass 2 dB up; 71 and 97 Hz came inside the envelope. SCORE 93.22 and 93.40 on two seeds; v3 re-read under the seven cuts 92.97 (seed 0 only). Variety 80.6 to 83.6, spectrum 95.7 to 96.6, recurrence 84.9 to 82.1. TWO BUILDS: (a) the clicks away through the run-down as well: its last quarters fell to -37.1 -37.9 and the clicks were 6 to 9 dB down just where they were meant to be heard thinning against the drum; 92.89 and 92.73. (b) in front while the clock runs down, the fillings whole to half-way: published. WHAT IS WEAK: the score's gain (0.25 to 0.4) is no more than the two seeds differ. SLOW is not proved: above 5 kHz the hat owns the band and I did not solo the clicks thinning against the drum. The wind-up still dips 3.6 dB at its third quarter, and the whole mix there is 3.5 dB under the page before (the four's other parts have gone): it does not swell. 114 Hz is still 8.7 under: the bass's commonest note is D2 (73 Hz), so that band is not its to fill. 547 and 641 Hz are 6.7 and 6.8 over. PUSH moved nothing I measured. Eleven novelty peaks stand between 0.11 and 0.15, inside the album's seven cuts, so the section count runs from 12 to 22 by cut. I cannot judge whether the second half's clicks read as walking away page by page or as fading under the four, nor whether 7 dB under the room is far or only blurred.
next: v5 on, every change behind a switch (v4 has away, home, slow, push, low on top of v3's eight and v2's six). (1) PROVE SLOW: solo three, five and seven over 1470 to 1575 sixteenths (367.5b to 393.75b) and read them beside the mix by quarter; if they are more than 10 dB under it, rest the hat for that stretch. One by-ear card after that: v3's run-down beside v4's, one clock slowing or clicks dropping out. (2) VARIETY is the lowest term (83.6: level range 4.9 dB, density 0.16): the second half's four pages all read -14.3. Give them a shape by rule, e.g. the four comes in a part a page again in the second half (drum; bass; hat; clap), or each page's first stretch is the drum and the clicks only. (3) THE STRETCH HEADS read 0.11 to 0.17 on the scorer, inside the cuts: make the chord an event (the drum rests the beat it lands on) or take it under 0.11. (4) THE WIND-UP's third quarter: bring the sixteenths in from -12, not -24, or let the bass stay to the half-way point. (5) AWAY in the second half: read the clicks alone over their room page by page (dr.sh with windows at 525b, 630b, 735b); if page 8 is under -7, hold it at 6. (6) 114 Hz: the drum's second harmonic (98 Hz) is the nearest thing; try its body peak at 110 in place of 130. (7) Re-render seam 2 for the mix plan: the last stretch changed again. v6, THE DRUM ANSWERS (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 13:20-13:33 GMT). Not heard by me. One switch (--without-knock; off is v5 byte for byte). THE IDEA: the second half's cycles of 3, 5 and 7 BEATS were never new. A click on a cycle of 3 sixteenths lands on the bass drum every 12 sixteenths, which is every 3 beats; the five every 5; the seven every 7. Those meetings were the only ones in the song that did nothing. KNOCK: from the first half's last page on (bar 79), when a click lands on the drum the drum answers with a low knock, a small kettledrum head (new patch lc-knock): G2 for the three, B flat 2 for the five, D3 for the seven. Under the last page of sixteenths a G minor triad is already turning in 3, 5 and 7 beats, all three notes together exactly where the page turns; through the run-down it is what is left with the drum; on the one the clicks take up those same cycles and the knock is the head of each. 299 knocks; none in the last four bars. BY SOLO, the knock alone: its partials on G2 98.0, 147.2, 194.3, 239.5 Hz (B flat 2 at 116.3, D3 at 146.9); it falls on exactly the beats that are multiples of 3, 5 or 7 (19 of the 32 read); highest sample -11.8 dBFS. Under the mix from 90 to 400 Hz: 7.1 dB on page 4, 5.6 in the run-down, 5.4 on page 5 (no bass), 7.4 on page 7. What it adds there, v6 less v5 by band: 90 to 105 Hz +2.0 to +2.7, 105 to 123 +1.2 to +2.2, 145 to 200 +1.9 to +4.6; the raw mix +0.8 to +1.5. Finished song: the one (two bars) -17.0 for -17.7; page 5 -17.4 for -17.9. WHAT IT TOOK: at 180 ms the head was a spike (-9.6 dBFS, 21 dB gone in 50 ms) with 13 dB less in its band than the bass: so it rings 800 ms, the spike is clipped off at -10 and the fader brings up the rest. At -4 dB it read 7 to 9 under the mix in its band; published at -2. SCORE 96.80 and 96.78 on two seeds; v5 re-read today 93.95. Spectrum 89.8 to 97.8: that is the song's hole from 90 to 200 Hz, filled by notes and not by an EQ. Recurrence 82.8 to 99.1: the scorer's small boundaries at the second half's stretch heads (0.11 to 0.15, inside the album's cuts) are gone, so it counts 14 to 9 sections for 19 to 12; that part is the scorer steadying, not music I can claim. Variety 90.5 to 86.3 (at the highest cut it now counts nine sections).
